picks.title: New documents raise more questions about Medicare’s AI prior-authorization experiment
picks.take: Medicare's AI prior-authorization experiment now has new documents and, naturally, more questions. Nothing says innovation like automating the denial pipeline first and asking about the guardrails in a follow-up edition.

picks.title: Oura to acquire Counsel Health for $625 million, placing a big bet on AI care
picks.take: A smart ring maker pays $625 million for a clinical AI startup after delaying its IPO. Your sleep score now comes with a differential diagnosis and, presumably, a subscription tier.

picks.title: Beyond the Rogue Agent-Preparing Health Systems for AI Failure
picks.take: JAMA suggests health systems prepare for AI failure, not just the dramatic rogue-agent kind. Radical idea: write the downtime procedure before the go-live party, not after the incident review.

picks.title: MDCalc launches a ‘rumble strip’ for doctors using generative AI tools
picks.take: MDCalc launches a 'rumble strip' for doctors using generative AI, which is reassuring, since nothing says autonomous clinical intelligence like needing the road to vibrate when you drift.

picks.title: Apple, OpenEvidence launch conversational health AI study and app
picks.take: Apple and OpenEvidence launch a conversational health AI study and app. Two giants collaborate to learn how people ask medical questions, a field previously studied by every waiting room and 2 a.m. search bar.

picks.title: Speak before the reveal: a practical method to protect clinical reasoning from artificial intelligence scribe deskilling, never-skilling, and mis-skilling
picks.take: A practical method asks clinicians to commit to their own reasoning before the AI scribe reveals its version. Finally, an intervention for deskilling that costs nothing and requires thinking, which is why it will need a task force.

picks.title: Opinion: AI’s health advice can be accurate and still make us sicker
picks.take: Researchers argue AI health advice can be factually accurate and still make people sicker by changing behavior. Accuracy was apparently the easy benchmark, which is why every vendor slide features it.

picks.title: Anthropic bought a one-person, AI-powered biotech: is this drug discovery's future?
picks.take: Anthropic buys a one-person, AI-powered biotech, and Nature asks whether this is drug discovery's future. Phase III trials remain famously unimpressed by pitch decks, but the acqui-hire has never looked leaner.

picks.title: Health AI spend doubles as providers invest in clinical copilots, front-office AI
picks.take: Health AI spending doubles as providers buy clinical copilots and front-office tools. Hospitals continue the proud tradition of investing aggressively in whatever might fix the paperwork they created.

picks.title: Healthcare struggles to scale AI past pilot stage: Google report
picks.take: A Google report says healthcare struggles to scale AI past the pilot stage. The pilot-to-production gap remains medicine's most reliable renewable resource, right after the pilot announcement press release.
